title: Laws Governing Photography, Filming, and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (Drones)
perspective: Egyptian Legal Framework & National Security Standards
summary: Egypt strictly regulates photography and visual recording to safeguard national security, sovereign infrastructure, and the dignity of its citizens.

sections.heading: Drone Regulations (Law No. 216 of 2017)
content: Absolute Ban without Defense Ministry Approval: The importation, manufacture, sale, possession, or operation of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (drones) of any size or weight is strictly prohibited under Law No. 216 of 2017 unless prior written authorization is issued directly by the Ministry of Defense.

Strict Penalties: Unauthorized possession or operation of a drone is classified as a severe offense against national security. Penalties range from imprisonment for 1 to 7 years and heavy fines (up to EGP 50,000 or more), along with immediate confiscation of the device.
Customs Enforcement: Customs authorities at all Egyptian land, sea, and air borders immediately seize unregistered drones upon entry.

sections.heading: Public Photography Regulations (Ministry of Tourism & Culture Decrees)
content: Personal Photography Rights: Street photography and personal tourist photography using standard handheld cameras or mobile phones in public areas are fully permitted and free of charge, provided public order and decorum are respected.

Strict Prohibitions: Photography of military bases, police checkpoints, government ministries, bridges, critical infrastructure, and security personnel is strictly illegal and subject to immediate legal prosecution.

Commercial Filming & Professional Equipment: Professional media setups (including tripods, professional lighting rigs, and specialized video gear) require official permits from the State Information Service (SIS) and relevant ministries.

Privacy & Respect: Taking photos of Egyptian citizens without their explicit verbal consent is illegal under Egyptian privacy laws. Publishing photographs that damage an individual's reputation or dignity is prohibited under the Penal Code.
